A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same dataset-bias study. All pages, figures, tables and appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched across the revised structure.

before.justification: v1 reports original dataset-classification experiments, representation-transfer results, corruption tests and a 20-participant user study, with additional experiments in Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds cross-dataset generalization experiments and a six-way classification confusion matrix.

M1.justification: The dataset-classification procedure, architectures and linear-probing approaches are retained. The added experiments use existing MoCo v3 and MAE methods for evaluation without introducing an algorithmic or architectural modification.

E1.justification: The original datasets remain, including the appendix ImageNet/ImageNetV2 comparison. Section 5.5 and Appendix B add cross-dataset evaluation of contrastive learning and masked reconstruction across all six source datasets, substantially extending the tested generalization scenarios.

E2.justification: The matched architecture and representation comparisons retain their comparator memberships in Tables 3, 7 and 8. The new cross-dataset tables compare training-data sources within MoCo v3 or MAE rather than introduce an additional competing algorithm.

E3.justification: v2 introduces source-by-target evaluation using MoCo v3 and MAE validation losses. Section 5.5 adds a combined-source control that holds total training-set size fixed by taking one-sixth from each dataset. Existing classification splits, training settings and user-study procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 5.5 and Appendix B add substantial analyses of distribution transfer and dataset mixing using two self-supervised objectives. Figure 7 adds classwise confusion analysis. The earlier corruption, memorization, scaling and training-curve analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports model-training seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The user-study histogram and mean/median reporting remain unchanged; the new loss tables and confusion matrix add no uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Tables 2-8 retain their results, including 84.7% YCD accuracy. New Tables 9 and 11 report cross-dataset losses, with combined-training averages of 1.871 for MoCo v3 and 0.376 for MAE. Figure 7 adds confusion values, but its diagonal averages 70.65% under the stated balanced sampling, inconsistent with Table 2's retained 69.2%. Figure 5's caption changes the human accuracy range from 40-70% to 40-60%, matching the unchanged histogram.

T1.justification: The N-way task definition and dataset-combination mathematics are unchanged. Neither version contains theoretical results or proofs, and v2 introduces no substantive mathematical derivation or formal assumption.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central claims that modern networks distinguish large datasets accurately and learn generalizable, transferable patterns beyond memorization. The added evidence and questions about dataset representativeness do not materially redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of cross-dataset loss gaps and controlled dataset mixing, distinguishes representativeness from social bias, and attributes DataComp/LAION confusion to shared sourcing and filtering. Appendix C repeats v1's uncertainty about the precise biases but newly specifies limited dataset coverage and the exclusion of video and language.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly specifies batch size 1024 for the cross-dataset MoCo v3 experiment and references its remaining hyperparameters; Section 5.5 documents the mixture control. Existing preprocessing, optimizer settings, linear-probing details and the code URL are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds works by Birhane, Mitchell, Koch and Raji and clarifies positioning concerning social fairness and pretraining versus benchmark datasets. The standalone Common Crawl reference is removed. The principal relationship to Torralba and Efros and Tommasi et al. remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites clarify the introduction, historical discussion and terminology. On Dataset Bias becomes a standalone section, and a limitations appendix is added. Most existing prose and the narrative order remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adopts an ICLR layout with widespread typography and display-placement changes. Figure 1 expands from 15 to 21 images, Figures 2-3 and Tables 5-6 are arranged side by side, and two loss tables plus a confusion matrix are added. Figure 7 also has an apparent row-label error: DataC. where ImageNet is expected.

improvement.justification: The controlled cross-dataset experiments provide useful evidence about transfer that v1 lacked, while the clarified meaning of bias and explicit coverage limitations improve interpretation. These gains are bounded: the new transfer tests use surrogate losses, and Figure 7 introduces a labeling error and an unexplained 70.65% versus 69.2% discrepancy. The established empirical case remains intact and receives a limited overall strengthening.
